related_resources.reason: Retrospective witness account of Trinity; transcript provenance and misquotation risks.
Charlotte Serber at Los Alamos and Leona Woods Marshall Libby at Chicago and Hanford; distinct sites and roles.
Technical and organizational history of wartime research including implosion program; source for institutional context rather than operational guidance.
Historical attribution to Neddermeyer, Kistiakowsky and others; technical details not needed in spoken lecture.
Scientist colleague and former Los Alamos theoretical-division head reflects on early physics, teaching and character; interpret retrospective appraisal accordingly.
Reconstructed group and regional exposure patterns with limitations on individual retrospective doses.
Nearby residents not warned; Trinity fallout and consequences. Does not establish exact exposures for individuals.
Oppenheimer family and social life at wartime Los Alamos; house and site history.
Pueblo, Athabaskan, Hispano and homesteader histories of Pajarito Plateau; wartime displacement and forced acquisition.
Tatlock medical education, politics, personal relationship with Oppenheimer, 1943 meeting under surveillance, and suicide in 1944; no invented motive.
Wartime organization, Groves, research community, Chevalier and Tatlock, Trinity, Japanese bombings and early postwar reactions; uses a mix of archival evidence and retrospective testimony.
Contemporary scientific panel acknowledges non-unanimity and rejects demonstration option; policy recommendation, not empirical proof.
